title: Telemetry-driven micro-slab GPU budgeting and adaptive headroom tuning
creator: Avery Chen
description: Implement a telemetry-driven micro-slab budgeting layer in the serving runtime that proactively carves transient GPU headroom for weights, KV cache, and activations. The goal is to reduce OOM events and tail latency during mixed workloads (interactive chat + batch embeddings) while minimizing reserved idle memory that adds cost. This ticket covers design, simulator, runtime allocator changes, and a staged rollout with observability and safety gates.
proposed_solution: Introduce a per-GPU micro-slab allocator that maintains small, time-decayed reservations (micro-slabs) across three logical pools: weights shadow (for quantized weights and occasional swaps), KV working set, and activation transient pool. Use continuous telemetry (KV occupancy histogram, activation peak samples, per-tenant recent batch footprints) to tune the size and decay rate of slabs. Implement a predictive headroom estimator using exponential smoothing of tail percentiles (p90/p95) and a conservative multiplier derived from tenant priority. On pressure, prefer safe activation eviction (compress + spill) and KV preemption windows rather than immediate weight paging. Expose runtime knobs: micro_slab_mode (off/baseline/adaptive), micro_slab_decay_ms, predictive_multiplier, and emergency_fallback_policy.
acceptance_criteria: New allocator integrated with serving runtime and respects micro_slab_mode toggles
Simulation harness shows reduction in OOM rate by >=60% on mixed workload traces used in benchmark fixtures
Token-latency p99 increase <= 5% vs baseline under same throughput in adaptive mode
Console dashboard surfaces KV occupancy heatmap, micro-slab utilization, and headroom recommendations
Canary rollout with 5% traffic has automatic rollback on increased OOM or latency SLO violations
rollout_plan: 1) Merge simulation and unit tests behind feature flag
2) Deploy allocator to canary fleet (~5 GPUs) with micro_slab_mode=baseline and detailed telemetry export
3) Run 72h canary, evaluate OOMs, tail latency, and cost proxy metrics
4) Enable adaptive mode for next canary cohort (25%); monitor for 7 days
5) Gradual ramp 25% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback and postmortem after each stage
tests: Unit: micro-slab eviction correctness and decay behavior
Integration: end-to-end model load + KV access under simulated multi-tenant bursts
Load: replay real traffic traces (customer anonymized) with mixed seq lengths
Chaos: force KV preemption and weight swap flaps to validate graceful fallback
risks: Aggressive decay could under-reserve and increase transient OOMs
Conservative multiplier could waste GPU memory and raise cost per token
Instrumentation overhead if telemetry sampling is too frequent
Interference with autoscaler heuristics if not coordinated (risk of oscillation)
